name: Elisha
bio:
Elisha son of Shaphat, of Abel Meholah, was named by the LORD at Horeb as the prophet who would succeed Elijah (1 Kings 19:15-16). Elijah found him plowing with twelve yoke of oxen, working the twelfth pair himself, and threw his cloak over him without a word. Elisha ran after Elijah asking only to first kiss his father and mother goodbye; Elijah's reply — "Go back again: for what have I done to thee?" — left the choice entirely his own. Elisha then slaughtered his own yoke of oxen, burned the plowing equipment to cook the meat, and gave it to the people to eat — a decisive break with his old life — before leaving to become Elijah's attendant (1 Kings 19:19-21).

## 📖 Core Story: Receiving Elijah's Mantle

On Elijah's last day, Elisha refused three times to leave his side as the LORD sent Elijah from Gilgal to Bethel, to Jericho, and to the Jordan, where Elijah parted the water with his cloak so the two could cross on dry ground. Asked what he wanted before Elijah was taken, Elisha requested a double portion of Elijah's spirit — a hard thing, Elijah told him, granted only if Elisha witnessed the taking. He did: a chariot and horses of fire appeared, Elijah went up in a whirlwind, and Elisha, crying "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof," tore his own clothes and took up Elijah's fallen cloak (2 Kings 2:1-12).

Elisha struck the Jordan with the cloak, asking, "Where is the LORD God of Elijah?" and the water parted for him just as it had for Elijah — proof to the watching sons of the prophets at Jericho that Elijah's spirit now rested on him, and they bowed before him (2 Kings 2:13-15). At Jericho, he healed the city's bad water by casting salt into its spring in the LORD's name (2 Kings 2:19-22). On the road up to Bethel, youths jeered at him, calling him "bald head"; he cursed them in the LORD's name, and two bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of them (2 Kings 2:23-24).
